content: The Save Huddersfield NHS campaign is a comprehensive initiative opposing the proposals by the Kirklees and Calderdale NHS Trust Board to close St. Luke's Hospital and relocate services, including maternity care, from Huddersfield to Halifax and Wakefield. This campaign is spearheaded by Dr. Jackie Grunsell. It originated following a public meeting organized by the Huddersfield branch of the Socialist Party of England and Wales. The campaign has undertaken various activities, including organizing a mock ballot on the issue, holding three demonstrations (the largest of which attracted over 2,000 participants), and collecting a petition signed by more than 60,000 individuals. One of the campaign's primary demands was for Kirklees Council to hold a referendum, allowing Huddersfield residents to decide on the matter. When the council declined to conduct such a referendum, the campaign fielded three candidates in the 2006 local government elections. Dr. Grunsell was elected to the council with a majority of 800 votes, framing her campaign as a referendum on the local council's actions. The campaign also collaborated with other groups nationwide under the umbrella of People United Saving Hospitals (PUSH). PUSH called for a national demonstration on Saturday, March 3, 2007, to protest against all NHS cuts. The group had already garnered support from AMICUS, Keep Our NHS Public, and two regions of UNISON. Previously, PUSH had organized a united day of action across the country on December 15, 2006, against NHS cuts. In addition to opposing the closure of St. Luke's Hospital, the campaign began addressing further threats to healthcare services in the district. These included the potential closure of Princess Royal Hospital, reductions in district nursing services, and a freeze on recruitment. In the 2007 local elections, the campaign fielded another candidate, Ian Slattery, in the Crosland Moor and Netherton ward of Kirklees Council. Although he did not win, he received over 1,000 votes. The threats to close Princess Royal Hospital have since been averted, partly due to the pressure exerted by the campaign. Near Princess Royal Hospital, located close to Greenhead Park, an unknown graffiti artist painted Save the NHS on the wall outside the hospital. Around the same time, a similar message was painted on the Labour Party offices, but it was quickly removed. However, the graffiti on the wall outside Princess Royal Hospital remains visible.
